key_insight: A finite spanwise-oscillating wall reduces turbulent boundary-layer drag by 32%, with exponential skin-friction onset and recovery length scales of 0.6δ and 0.9δ.
engineering_relevance: The measured response lengths can inform actuator placement and sizing for localized turbulent drag control.
method: Study a turbulent boundary layer at Reτ = 652 with wall oscillation period T+ ≈ 101 and amplitude A+ ≈ 7.
Estimate local skin friction using arctangent-based nonlinear regression of near-wall data.
Track turbulence statistics and conditional quadrant events across control onset and recovery.
evidence_signal: The skin-friction estimation method was assessed against reference DNS data and reproduced experimental measurement-error trends; most Reynolds-stress responses had exponential length scales within 0.5δ, except the slower shear-stress peak.
watch_item: The reported drag reduction does not establish net energy savings after accounting for wall-actuation power.
paper_title: Spatially developing drag reduction across a finite oscillating wall
